Wheel-arch flares and Hooker side pipes have been added, and the van also features chrome bumpers, a horizontal grille, porthole side windows, tinted glass, a sliding passenger-side rear door, a roof vent, and roof rails.
The sleeping platform at the rear of the cabin is shown above along with a variety of accompanying Elvis Presley memorabilia. The 350ci V8 is augmented by an Edelbrock intake manifold and an Edelbrock AVS four-barrel carburetor. Power is delivered to the rear wheels via a three-speed automatic transmission. The vehicle was featured in the March 1984 issue of Vans & Trucks magazine, a copy of which is included in the sale.

In the late 2010s, the vehicle was stripped and its graphics were reapplied, with the highlights and mural work performed by Jason Brookshire of B Street Paintworks following refurbishment work by Wild Cherry Customs. Wheel-arch flares and Hooker side pipes have been added, and the van also features chrome bumpers, a horizontal grille, porthole side windows, tinted glass, a sliding passenger-side rear door, a roof vent, and roof rails.
